items.question: Which Republic Act is known as the 'Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016' that strengthened and modernized the practice of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering?
items.rationale: R.A. 10915 lapsed into law on July 21, 2016, repealing R.A. 8559 and aligning ABE practice with international standards.

items.question: When was Republic Act No. 3927, the original Philippine Agricultural Engineering Law, approved and enacted?
items.rationale: R.A. 3927 was enacted on June 18, 1964 (31 sections), later repealed by R.A. 8559 (1998) and R.A. 10915 (2016).

items.question: Which Philippine law promotes the development and adoption of modern, appropriate, and cost-effective agricultural and fisheries machinery and equipment?
items.rationale: R.A. 10601 (Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Law of 2013) governs mechanization, machinery registration, and BAFE.

items.question: Under R.A. 10601, BAFE requires registration of agricultural and fisheries machinery entities abbreviated as MFADDIE. What does MFADDIE stand for?
items.answer: Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Distributor, Dealer, Importer, and Exporter
items.rationale: All entities engaged in manufacturing, fabricating, assembling, distributing, dealing, importing, or exporting agri-fishery machinery must register with BAFE.
choices: Manufacturer, Foreign Assembler, Distribution, Dealer, Investor, and Employer
Machinery Firm, Assembler, Designer, Dealer, Inspector, and Engineer
Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Distributor, Dealer, Importer, and Exporter
Mechanization Facility, Agency, Distributor, Developer, Importer, and Exporter

items.question: Under R.A. 10915, how often must a licensed Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer renew their Professional Identification Card (PIC) with the PRC?
items.rationale: The PRC Professional Identification Card (PIC) is valid for 3 years and renewed upon paying fees and submitting CPD compliance and AIPO (PSABE) Certificate of Good Standing.

items.question: Which of the following are required for the renewal of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer's Professional Identification Card (PIC)?
items.answer: CPD units and Certificate of Good Standing from the AIPO (PSABE)
items.rationale: Section 20 of R.A. 10915 requires proof of CPD credit units and a Certificate of Good Standing from the Accredited Integrated Professional Organization (PSABE).
choices: CPD units and Certificate of Good Standing from the AIPO (PSABE)
Endorsement from the Department of Agriculture
A new passing score on the board exam
Only payment of PRC renewal fees

items.subtopic: 1.0 ABE vs. CE Scope of Practice
items.question: Under R.A. 10915, which of the following infrastructure projects falls strictly within the signing and sealing authority of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer rather than a general municipal barangay road?
items.answer: Farm-to-market roads (FMR), communal irrigation, and agricultural slaughterhouses
items.rationale: ABEs sign and seal plans and specifications for FMRs, irrigation and drainage systems, farm structures, and agri-processing facilities.
choices: Farm-to-market roads (FMR), communal irrigation, and agricultural slaughterhouses

items.subtopic: 1.0 ABE vs. ChE Scope of Practice
items.question: How does the scope of practice of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer (ABE) differ from that of a Chemical Engineer (ChE) in processing plants?
items.answer: ABEs handle primary agricultural/bioprocess systems and farm-level value-adding, while ChEs handle industrial chemical plants
items.rationale: Under R.A. 10915, ABEs cover agricultural bioprocess, postharvest, and farm waste systems, whereas industrial chemical manufacturing belongs to ChEs.
choices: ABEs are prohibited from designing food dryers or grain mills
There is no legal distinction between the two professions

items.question: Who is primarily responsible for calibrating, integrating, and preparing technical specifications of agricultural sensors and controlled-environment instrumentation used in precision farming?
items.rationale: Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation, and Control Systems is a core competency area under R.A. 10915 and the PRC ABELE TOS.

items.question: Presidential Decree No. 1594 (later superseded by R.A. 9184) originally prescribed policies, guidelines, rules, and regulations for which of the following?
items.rationale: P.D. 1594 governed government infrastructure project procurement, bidding, and contracts prior to the Government Procurement Reform Act (R.A. 9184).

items.question: What does CPES stand for in the evaluation of government agricultural infrastructure construction projects?
items.rationale: CPES evaluates contractor performance during and upon completion of government infrastructure projects (workmanship, materials, time, facilities, etc.).
choices: Civil and Agricultural Planning Evaluation Scheme

items.question: Under Philippine environmental regulations (R.A. 8749 / DENR-EMB), what document must an agri-processing facility with air pollution source equipment (such as a rice hull furnace or boiler) secure before operating?
items.rationale: A Permit to Operate (PTO) Air Pollution Source Installations (APSI) is issued by DENR-EMB to ensure emissions comply with Clean Air Act standards.

items.question: Under R.A. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000), which unit is primarily mandated to establish Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and implement segregated collection at the community level?
items.rationale: R.A. 9003 places primary responsibility for solid waste segregation, MRFs, and 10-year solid waste management plans on LGUs and barangays.

items.question: According to the 2013 PHilMech study, what was the average level of agricultural mechanization in the Philippines for all crops, and specifically for rice farms?
items.rationale: PHilMech's 2013 benchmark established 1.23 hp/ha across all crops and 2.31 hp/ha for rice cultivation.

items.question: Which stage of agricultural evolution is characterized by the integration of IoT sensors, AI, drones, cloud computing, and autonomous robotics for real-time precision farm management?
items.rationale: Ag 1.0 = manual/animal labor; Ag 2.0 = mechanization & chemical inputs (Green Revolution); Ag 3.0 = GPS/precision guidance; Ag 4.0 = IoT, AI, big data, and smart autonomous farming.

items.question: Which historical phase of farming corresponds to Agriculture 2.0?
items.answer: Widespread adoption of tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding varieties
items.rationale: Agriculture 2.0 (mid-20th century / Green Revolution) introduced internal combustion tractors, synthetic fertilizers, pesticides, and improved crop varieties.
choices: Autonomous swarm robotics and digital twins
Subsistence farming using hand tools and draft animals
Widespread adoption of tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding varieties

items.question: Which statement best distinguishes digitalization, automation, and robotics in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering?
items.answer: Digitalization converts farm data to digital form; automation executes tasks without continuous human intervention; robotics uses programmable physical machines to sense and act
items.rationale: Digitalization handles data capture/processing, automation handles self-regulating control loops, and robotics combines electromechanical actuation with sensing.
choices: Automation and digitalization mean exactly the same thing
Robotics only refers to software spreadsheets
Digitalization converts farm data to digital form; automation executes tasks without continuous human intervention; robotics uses programmable physical machines to sense and act

items.question: What does the DA-BAFE platform 'GeoAgri' stand for?
items.answer: Geographic Information System for Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Infrastructure

items.question: In a standard Geographic Information System (GIS) coordinate plane, what does the x-coordinate (Easting) represent?
items.rationale: In GIS and Cartesian mapping, x represents East–West horizontal position (longitude/easting) and y represents North–South position (latitude/northing).

items.question: What does ROPS stand for on four-wheel agricultural tractors?
items.rationale: ROPS is a cab or frame structure engineered to protect tractor operators from crush injuries during tractor overturns.

items.question: During performance testing of a heated-air mechanical grain dryer per PAES, at what regular time interval are temperature, relative humidity, and grain moisture readings typically recorded?
items.answer: Every 30 minutes (or 1 hour depending on dryer batch duration)
items.rationale: PAES 202 (Methods of Test for Heated-Air Mechanical Grain Dryers) specifies periodic 30-minute to 1-hour sampling intervals for air conditions and moisture tracking.
choices: Only at the start and end of the test
Every 30 minutes (or 1 hour depending on dryer batch duration)

items.question: Which of the following is classified as a primary tillage implement designed to cut, invert, and break deep soil layers?
items.rationale: Moldboard, disk, chisel, and subsoiler plows are primary tillage implements; harrows and cultipackers are secondary tillage implements.

items.question: What is the primary function of the intake and exhaust valves in a four-stroke internal combustion engine?
items.answer: To admit fresh air/air-fuel mixture into the cylinder and release burned exhaust gases at precise timings

items.question: Crude oil (petroleum) is primarily a complex mixture of which class of chemical compounds?
items.rationale: Crude oil consists mainly of hydrogen and carbon compounds (alkanes, cycloalkanes, and aromatic hydrocarbons).

items.question: When shifting a standard manual-transmission agricultural tractor from first gear to a higher gear, which pedal must the operator depress first?
items.rationale: Depressing the clutch disengages engine power from the transmission so gears can shift smoothly without grinding.

items.question: An NIA irrigation drop/waterfall has a discharge of 1.5 m³/s and a gross head of 8 m. What is the theoretical hydraulic power available (use γ = 9.81 kN/m³)?

What is the speed ratio of the engine and the shredder pulleys?
items.rationale:
Given:
Shredder pulley - 5 inches
Engine pulley - 4 inches
Engine speed - 2400 rpm
Required: Shredder speed and speed ratio
N1 D1 = N2 D2
N1 = N2 D2 / D1
= (2400 rpm × 4 inches) / 5 inches
= 1,920 rpm
Nr = N2 / N1
= 2,400 rpm / 1,920 rpm
= 1.25

= 12.5 m³/hr

= 60 ft / (3.28 ft/m)
= 18.3 m

= 1.4 hp

items.question: In sandy or very loose soils where embankment stability is critical, what is the flattest recommended side slope (H:V) commonly cited for unlined earth canals?
items.rationale: Very loose sand or peat soils require flat side slopes up to 3:1 or 4:1 (H:V) to prevent sloughing and bank collapse.

items.question: Which irrigation conveyance structure carries canal water under pressure beneath a road, railway, or natural depression?
items.rationale: An inverted siphon conveys water below an obstruction using closed conduit flow under hydrostatic head.

items.question: A concrete gravity dam primarily resists horizontal hydrostatic water pressure through which mechanism?
items.answer: Its own massive weight acting downward

items.question: Which rainfall lifting mechanism occurs when moist air masses are forced upward as they encounter a mountain barrier?
items.rationale: Orographic lifting is mountain-facilitated; convective lifting is caused by localized thermal heating; frontal lifting occurs along warm/cold air-mass boundaries.

items.question: A spillway is designed for a 25-year return period flood. What is the probability that this design flood will be equaled or exceeded in any single year?
items.rationale: Annual exceedance probability P = 1 / T = 1 / 25 = 0.04 = 4%.

items.rationale: ETc = Kc × ETo = 1.20 × 5.5 mm/day = 6.60 mm/day.

items.question: A soil has a Field Capacity (FC) of 24% and Permanent Wilting Point (PWP) of 16% by weight. What is its present moisture content if 25% of its available moisture (AM) has been used?
items.rationale: AM = FC − PWP = 24% − 16% = 8%; Moisture used = 0.25 × 8% = 2%; Present MC = 24% − 2% = 22%.

items.question: Which form of soil water drains downward freely under the pull of gravity between saturation and field capacity?
items.rationale: Gravitational water occupies macropores above field capacity (0 to 1/3 atm) and drains freely downward.

items.question: If the readily available moisture (RAM) in a crop's root zone is 48 mm and the peak daily crop water use (ETc) is 6 mm/day, what is the irrigation interval?
items.rationale: Irrigation Interval = RAM / ETc = 48 mm ÷ 6 mm/day = 8 days.

items.question: A paddy field has ETc = 6 mm/day, percolation = 2 mm/day, effective rainfall = 1.5 mm/day, and application efficiency = 75%. What is the Farm Irrigation Requirement (FIR)?

items.question: Estimate the runoff volume in cubic meters from a 10-hectare drainage basin if rainfall depth for 6 hours reached 60 mm and duration of runoff is 10 hours. Use a triangular hydrograph and typical runoff coefficient of 0.35.
items.rationale:
1,800 m³
Determining rainfall intensity I
I = Rainfall depth / Rainfall duration
= 60 mm / 6 hrs
= 10 mm/hr
Determining Peak Runoff Rate, q
q = 0.0028CIA
= 0.0028 (0.35)(10 mm/hr)(10 has)
= 0.1 cubic meters/second
Determining Total Runoff Volume Q
Using a Triangular Hydrograph
Q = 0.5 × Height of the triangle x Base of the triangle
Q = 0.5 × Peak runoff rate x Runoff duration
= 0.5qT
= 0.5 (0.1 m³/s) (10 hrs × 3600 s/hr)
= 1,800 m³

items.question: given the following:(exact given)
From Dr. Tambong: What is the top width at water surface level of the most efficient concrete open channel if the design depth is 5 meters? The design discharge is 100 m³/s and velocity is 2 m/s
items.rationale:
12.9 m
Hint: If the canal is a trapezoidal concrete and side angle is not given, then it is a Most Efficient Canal (in which Ө = 60º and z = 0.577). Specifying it as most efficient canal is often omitted in the board question.
Q = AV
100 = A (2)
A = 50 m²
tan Ө = 1 / z
tan 60 º = 1 / z
1.732 = 1 / z
z = 0.577
A = bd + zd2
A-zd2 = bd
b = (A-zd2) / d
= [50 − 0.577(5)²] / 5
= 7.12 m
t = b + (2d / tan Ө)
= 7.12 m + [2(5) / 1.732]
= 12.89 m
Checking 1 (To boost Confidence but don’t do checking in actual exam):
A = bd + zd2
50 = (7.12)(5) + 0.577(5)²
50 = 35.6 + 14.4
50 = 50
Checking 2:
A = d [(t + b)/2]
50 = 5 [(12.89 + 7.12)/2]
50 = 5[10]
50 = 50
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS; Tambong Subject B Part 1

1,000 liters water, 20 liters insecticide
Water vol. = Area in m² × Water mixing rate

= 1,000 liters

items.question: Estimate the number of kilograms of urea fertilizer are to be applied per hectare using 46 − 0 − 0 urea fertilizer alone. The recommended rate of nitrogen is 90 kg/hectare.
items.rationale:
196
Computation procedure:
To determine the fertilizer rate for a particular nutrient, multiply the rate of the desired nutrient by 100 and divide by the percentage of the nutrient in the fertilizer (Manitoba Soil Fertility Guide, 2022).
Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient × 100) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer
= (90 kg/ha × 100) / 46
= 195.7 kg/ha

items.question: Determine the number of bags of urea fertilizer needed per hectare using 46 − 0 − 0 urea containing 50 kilograms per bag. The recommended rate of nitrogen is 90 kg/hectare.
items.rationale:
5
Computation procedure: To obtain the number of bags of fertilizer, divide the fertilizer requirement in kg/hectare by the number of kilograms contained per bag, then round up (not round off) to the nearest integer.
Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient × 100) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer
= (90 kg/ha × 100) / 46
= 195.65 kg/ha
No. of Bags = Fertilizer Requirement in kg/hectare / No. of Kilograms Contained per Bag
= 195.65 kg/ha / 50 kg/bag

items.question: Regression analysis conducted reveal that rice yield is governed by the function y = x² - 8x + 3 where y is the yield and x is the numbers bags of urea applied per hectare. To maximize yield, what should be the number of bags/ha of urea applied?
items.rationale:
4 bags/ha
To maximize y, set the derivative dy/dx = 0
y = x² - 8x + 3
Using power rule in derivation & since the derivative of a constant is zero,
dy/dx = (2)x²-1 − 8(1) × 1 − 1 + 0
dy/dx = 2x - 8 + 0
but dy/dx = 0, hence
2x - 8 + 0 = 0
2x = 8
x = 8/2
x = 4 bags/ha

items.rationale: For water/ice at 0°C, the latent heat (enthalpy) of fusion is approximately 334 kJ/kg (144 BTU/lb).

items.question: What is the theoretical (Carnot) Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a refrigerator operating between an evaporator temperature of −20°C (253 K) and a condenser temperature of 40°C (313 K)?
A cold storage refrigeration unit removes 18 kW of heat from a vegetable room while its compressor consumes 4.5 kW of electrical power. What is its COP?
items.rationale: COP = Q_L / W_in = 18 kW / 4.5 kW = 4.0.

items.question: In a vapor-compression refrigeration system, which component absorbs heat from the cold storage space as the liquid refrigerant boils into vapor?
items.rationale: The evaporator absorbs heat inside the cooled space; the condenser rejects heat to the outside environment.

items.question: Dry ice, commonly used for ultra-cold shipping of perishable biological and food products, is the solid form of which compound?
items.rationale: Dry ice is solid CO₂, which sublimates directly from solid to gas at −78.5°C under atmospheric pressure.

items.question: In a flatbed or recirculating grain dryer, what is the function of the plenum chamber?

To hull and polish brown rice

items.question: In rice processing, 'milling degree' measures the extent of bran removal from brown rice. Which type of threshing cylinder is most commonly used in Philippine axial-flow rice threshers?
items.rationale: Peg-tooth cylinders are standard for local rice threshers, while rasp-bar cylinders are common in combine harvesters for wheat/corn/rice.

items.subtopic: 3.0 Primary Component of Plant Cell Walls
items.question: Which biopolymer is the most abundant structural component of plant cell walls?
items.rationale: Plant cell walls are composed primarily of cellulose microfibrils embedded in hemicellulose and lignin.

items.question: Approximately how many kilograms of stoichiometric air are required for the complete combustion of 1 kg of dry rice hull?
items.rationale: Rice hull has a stoichiometric air-to-fuel ratio of approximately 4.7 kg air per kg fuel (compared to ~14.7 for gasoline/diesel).

items.question: In biomass gasification and combustion, what is the equivalence ratio (φ) defined as?
items.answer: Actual air-to-fuel ratio divided by the stoichiometric air-to-fuel ratio
items.rationale: Gasification typically operates at an equivalence ratio of 0.25–0.40 (30–40% of stoichiometric air).
choices: Mass of ash divided by mass of fuel
Actual air-to-fuel ratio divided by the stoichiometric air-to-fuel ratio
Output electrical energy divided by input thermal energy
Heating value divided by moisture content

items.question: What is the seventh (final) principle of the Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) food safety system?
items.rationale: The 7 HACCP principles end with establishing comprehensive record-keeping and documentation procedures.

items.question: Under PAES 418:2002 (Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetable), the temporary raw material storage area shall have a minimum capacity for how many days of operation?
items.rationale: PAES 418 specifies 2–5 days of temporary raw material storage capacity to buffer supply and processing schedules.

items.question: What is the primary goal of Republic Act No. 10068 (Organic Agriculture Act of 2010)?
items.answer: To promote, propagate, develop further, and implement the practice of organic agriculture in the Philippines

items.question: Under PAES 413:2001 (Biogas Plant), anaerobic digestion operating in the mesophilic temperature range (30–40°C) typically requires what hydraulic retention time for animal manure?
items.rationale: Mesophilic digestion (~35°C) balances gas yield and digester volume at ~20–30 days retention time.

items.question: A swine farm has 200 head of porkers, each producing 2.2 kg of manure/day with a specific biogas yield of 0.06 m³/kg manure. Estimate daily biogas production using P = NMG.
items.rationale: P = N × M × G = 200 × 2.2 kg/day × 0.06 m³/kg = 26.4 m³/day.

items.subtopic: 3.0 Slurry, Sludge, and Scum in Biogas Digesters
items.question: In an anaerobic biogas digester, what is the floating fibrous crust that forms on top of the liquid substrate called?
items.rationale: Slurry is the manure-water mixture; sludge settles at the bottom; scum is the floating fibrous layer on top that can block gas release if not stirred.

items.question: Under R.A. 9003, what is the contaminated liquid produced when water percolates through decomposing solid waste in a landfill or dump?
items.rationale: Leachate contains dissolved and suspended pollutants and must be collected and treated to prevent groundwater contamination.

items.question: Per PAES 414-2:2002 (Agricultural Solid Waste – Composting), what is the optimum thermophilic temperature inside a compost pile to effectively destroy pathogens and weed seeds?
items.rationale: Maintaining ~55°C during the active thermophilic phase sanitizes pathogens without killing beneficial composting microbes.

items.question: Under PAES 232:2017 (Water Re-use for Irrigation), what is the maximum allowable 5-day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD₅) threshold for treated wastewater used in crop irrigation?
items.rationale: PAES 232 sets BOD₅ ≤ 150 mg/L for agricultural wastewater reuse to protect soil aeration and crop health.

items.question: What is the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) established under the Kyoto Protocol?
items.answer: A market mechanism allowing industrialized nations to invest in greenhouse gas emission-reduction projects (like biogas) in developing countries to earn carbon credits
items.rationale: CDM enables projects such as methane capture from livestock biogas plants to earn Certified Emission Reduction (CER) credits.
choices: A mechanical cleaning device for rice mills
A market mechanism allowing industrialized nations to invest in greenhouse gas emission-reduction projects (like biogas) in developing countries to earn carbon credits

items.question: In an AC induction motor, what is the stationary outer assembly of laminated iron core and copper windings that creates the rotating magnetic field?

items.rationale:
50 sq. mm TW copper wire with 98.4 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature
Refer to PAES 129:2002.
From Philippine Electrical Code 2000, Article 4.30 Section 2.2 (a), “Branch-circuit conductors that supply a single motor used in a continuous duty application shall have an ampacity of not less than 125 percent of the motor’s full-load current rating.”
Minimum Ampacity = Full load current × 125%
Minimum Ampacity = 68 Amperes × 1.25
Minimum Ampacity = 85 Amperes
The only conductor with allowable ampacity equal or more than 85 Amperes is recommended to use.
